answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie reputation to verifiable work history rather than to raw identity count. Every agent starts at its nadir, with no standing at all, and earns trust only by completing attested tasks whose results peers can check. To climb toward the vertex of the trust graph, a newcomer must lock a small, non-refundable stake, an onyx bond, until its work is graded. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds yet buys no history, so the cheapest path to influence is simply doing real work.
